title: Wolves 0 Tottenham 1 – Has Palhinha just kept Spurs’ chances of avoiding relegation alive?
content:
Tottenham Hotspur remain two points adrift of safety despite Joao Palhinha’s late goal earning them victory against Wolves and a first Premier League win of 2026.

Spurs looked in serious trouble after Nottingham Forest’s thumping 5-0 victory over Sunderland on Friday increased their lead over them to eight points. When West Ham took the lead against Everton in their own 3pm Saturday kick-off, it served to extend the live gap to Roberto De Zerbi’s side to four points.

Tottenham briefly jumped out of the drop zone in the live table when Palhinha scored on 82 minutes and Everton then equalised at the London Stadium on 88 minutes, sending the travelling Spurs fans into wild celebrations at Molineux. But Callum Wilson’s added-time winner for West Ham lifted them back up to 17th, two points clear of Spurs with four games to play.

Tottenham did avoid equalling their worst winless run in league history, a 16-game stretch in 1935, but worrying-looking injuries that forced off key attacking players Dominic Solanke and Xavi Simons will add to their problems.

The Athletic’s Jay Harris breaks down the key moments.

They are in a bad situation, but have been given a small glimmer of hope.

Palhinha’s late goal today earned them their first win in the Premier League since December. The injuries to Solanke and Simons will make their escape act more difficult, but the psychological impact of finally beating someone should be huge.

Spurs started brightly against Wolves but their intensity dropped off after the first 15 minutes. That was summed up by striker Randal Kolo Muani, who initially caused Hugo Bueno problems and then was anonymous for the rest of the first half. It was no surprise head coach De Zerbi replaced the Frenchman with Mathys Tel at the break.

One of Spurs’ biggest problems this season has been their inability to create high-quality chances. They should be desperately fighting for their lives but offered very little threat in open play at Molineux. Rodrigo Bentancur’s header from Pedro Porro’s corner in the second half was their best opportunity until Palhinha scored just when it felt like all hope was lost.

The Portuguese’s scrappy effort sparked a wild few minutes in the battle to avoid the drop.

Back in London, Dewsbury-Hall’s 88th-minute equaliser briefly gave Everton hope of a draw with West Ham. If Spurs had lost and West Ham had won, De Zerbi’s side would have been in a perilous position.

It looked like the momentum was about to swing massively in Spurs’ favour and they were, for a blissful few minutes, out of the bottom three on goal difference. Then already-relegated Wolves’ fans started taunting the opposition fans and chanting “Tottenham away, ole ole!” — indicating the clubs would be meeting in next season’s Championship. A few seconds later, the news filtered through that West Ham had retaken the lead.

Still, there were huge celebrations off the bench and in the away section after Antonin Kinsky’s fine late save ensured a big win.

Spurs have been struck by a horrible injury curse over the past two seasons. It feels like every time one player returns from the treatment room, somebody else takes his place.

James Maddison suffered an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) knee injury in pre-season. Dejan Kulusevski is still recovering from a complicated knee problem which Tottenham’s then head coach Ange Postecoglou originally referred to as a “knock” last year. Maddison and Kulusevski have not played a single minute for the club this season.

Mohammed Kudus has suffered a setback in his return from a hamstring issue, while Destiny Udogie is back on the sidelines only a few weeks after recovering from the same ailment.

Spurs’ injury curse took a new cruel twist on Saturday afternoon. Solanke was substituted just before half-time after dropping to the floor off the ball a couple of minutes after making a tackle on Wolves’ midfielder Andre. He appeared to be rubbing the back of his left leg.

Solanke has endured a difficult time at Spurs since he joined them from Bournemouth in August 2024 for a club-record fee, but remains one of their most influential players. Losing the England international for any period of time over the run-in damages their chances of avoiding relegation and his own quest to play at this summer’s World Cup.

What happened with Simons in the second half looked even more ominous.

The 22-year-old Netherlands international went down holding his right knee after chasing the ball and colliding with Bueno. He tried to continue and even waved towards the bench in anger when he was replaced by Palhinha. However, Simons had to be carried around the pitch towards the dressing room on a stretcher a couple of minutes later.

He was nearly Spurs’ matchwinner in last weekend’s 2-2 home draw with Brighton & Hove Albion and had been exceptional in the second leg of their Champions League quarter-finals exit to Atletico Madrid in March. Simons has been the only player to provide a creative spark and now it looks like he could miss the final few games of the season.

Losing one of their best attacking players would have left Tottenham in a difficult spot. Losing two in the same game will leave them numb.

A lot of the credit for Palhinha’s goal should actually go to Tel. The France Under-21 international chased the ball when it looked like it was going out of play. He prevented Wolves earning a goal kick and Spurs kept possession until they won a corner.

One out-swinging Porro delivery led to a great chance for Bentancur a few minutes before Palhinha scored, and Wolves did not learn their lesson. The ball was allowed to drop inside the box and Richarlison scuffed a left-footed effort towards goal. The effort was going wide until the Portuguese midfielder poked the ball into the net at the front post.

It is the second time this season Palhinha has saved Spurs from a damaging result against Wolves. In September, his stoppage-time effort earned a point under then head coach Thomas Frank and prevented an embarrassing 1-0 home defeat.

If Simons’ curling strike against Brighton last weekend was worthy of winning any game, Palhinha’s goal today was at the opposite end of the scale. It was scrappy and scruffy, but nobody of a Tottenham persuasion cared. He jumped over the advertising hoardings to celebrate with the travelling Spurs fans. De Zerbi leapt up and down on the touchline. Minutes later, the final whistle confirmed Spurs had scraped over the line to end a 15-game winless run.

De Zerbi recognised the significance of the moment by bringing on defender Radu Dragusin for midfielder Conor Gallagher in the final few minutes. Then Kinksy clattered into a post making a fantastic save from Joao Gomes’ free kick on one of the last plays of the game.

This group of players have finally shown their supporters that they are up for the challenge and prepared to fight to stay in the division. There may be injuries, but there is also hope.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi said of their victory: “We played 30, 35 minutes very well in the first half. We didn’t create many chances, but we had control. (In the second half) maybe (because of) the pressure to win this game, we didn’t play well, but today the three points was very important. We can (now) prepare for the next four games.”

He was happy with his players’ mental approach to the match but wants them to be better in possession: “We have to play, we can’t lose our style or lose the order on the pitch — we can’t show the quality of the players if we play like we did in the second half, but in terms of attitude and spirit, (a) great 90 minutes. Without the ball, we can’t win the game. These players are good enough to win with the ball. We can play much better than the second half.”

Regarding Dominic Solanke and Xavi Simons having to go off, De Zerbi added: “I spoke with the doctor but they don’t understand (the severity of the injuries yet). They have to see the players on Monday and Tuesday.”
